NKJV.1: Now when Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled from the house of Judah and Benjamin one hundred and eighty thousand chosen men who were warriors, to fight against Israel, that he might restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
NKJV.2: But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
NKJV.3: “Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying,
NKJV.4: ‘Thus says the LORD: “You shall not go up or fight against your brethren! Let every man return to his house, for this thing is from Me.” ’ ” Therefore they obeyed the words of the LORD, and turned back from attacking Jeroboam.
NKJV.5: So Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and built cities for defense in Judah.
NKJV.6: And he built Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
NKJV.10: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and Benjamin, fortified cities.
NKJV.11: And he fortified the strongholds, and put captains in them, and stores of food, oil, and wine.
NKJV.12: Also in every city he put shields and spears, and made them very strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side.
NKJV.13: And from all their territories the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel took their stand with him.
NKJV.14: For the Levites left their common-lands and their possessions and came to Judah and Jerusalem, for Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests to the LORD.
NKJV.15: Then he appointed for himself priests for the high places, for the demons, and the calf idols which he had made.
NKJV.16: And after the Levites left, those from all the tribes of Israel, such as set their heart to seek the LORD God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD God of their fathers.
NKJV.17: So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong for three years, because they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.
NKJV.18: Then Rehoboam took for himself as wife Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and of Abihail the daughter of Eliah the son of Jesse.
NKJV.19: And she bore him children: Jeush, Shamariah, and Zaham.
NKJV.20: After her he took Maachah the granddaughter of Absalom; and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
NKJV.21: Now Rehoboam loved Maachah the granddaughter of Absalom more than all his wives and his concubines; for he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and begot twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
NKJV.22: And Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maachah as chief, to be leader among his brothers; for he intended to make him king.
NKJV.23: He dealt wisely, and dispersed some of his sons throughout all the territories of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city; and he gave them provisions in abundance. He also sought many wives for them.

ESV.1: When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, 180,000 chosen warriors, to fight against Israel, to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
ESV.2: But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God:
ESV.3: “Say to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin,
ESV.4: ‘Thus says the LORD, You shall not go up or fight against your relatives. Return every man to his home, for this thing is from me.’” So they listened to the word of the LORD and returned and did not go against Jeroboam.
ESV.5: Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built cities for defense in Judah.
ESV.10: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, fortified cities that are in Judah and in Benjamin.
ESV.11: He made the fortresses strong, and put commanders in them, and stores of food, oil, and wine.
ESV.12: And he put shields and spears in all the cities and made them very strong. So he held Judah and Benjamin.
ESV.13: And the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel presented themselves to him from all places where they lived.
ESV.14: For the Levites left their common lands and their holdings and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons cast them out from serving as priests of the LORD,
ESV.15: and he appointed his own priests for the high places and for the goat idols and for the calves that he had made.
ESV.16: And those who had set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel came after them from all the tribes of Israel to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
ESV.17: They strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and for three years they made Rehoboam the son of Solomon secure, for they walked for three years in the way of David and Solomon.
ESV.18: Rehoboam took as wife Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and of Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse,
ESV.19: and she bore him sons, Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
ESV.20: After her he took Maacah the daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.

ESV.22: And Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah as chief prince among his brothers, for he intended to make him king.
ESV.23: And he dealt wisely and distributed some of his sons through all the districts of Judah and Benjamin, in all the fortified cities, and he gave them abundant provisions and procured wives for them.

NLT.1: When Rehoboam arrived at Jerusalem, he mobilized the men of Judah and Benjamin — 180,000 select troops — to fight against Israel and to restore the kingdom to himself.
NLT.2: But the LORD said to Shemaiah, the man of God,
NLT.3: “Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin:
NLT.4: ‘This is what the LORD says: Do not fight against your relatives. Go back home, for what has happened is my doing!’” So they obeyed the message of the LORD and did not fight against Jeroboam.
NLT.5: Rehoboam remained in Jerusalem and fortified various towns for the defense of Judah.
NLT.6: He built up Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
NLT.10: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. These became the fortified towns of Judah and Benjamin.
NLT.11: Rehoboam strengthened their defenses and stationed commanders in them, and he stored supplies of food, olive oil, and wine.
NLT.12: He also put shields and spears in these towns as a further safety measure. So only Judah and Benjamin remained under his control.
NLT.13: But all the priests and Levites living among the northern tribes of Israel sided with Rehoboam.
NLT.14: The Levites even abandoned their pasturelands and property and moved to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons would not allow them to serve the LORD as priests.
NLT.15: Jeroboam appointed his own priests to serve at the pagan shrines, where they worshiped the goat and calf idols he had made.
NLT.16: From all the tribes of Israel, those who sincerely wanted to worship the LORD, the God of Israel, followed the Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
NLT.17: This strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and for three years they supported Rehoboam son of Solomon, for during those years they faithfully followed in the footsteps of David and Solomon.
NLT.18: Rehoboam married his cousin Mahalath, the daughter of David’s son Jerimoth and of Abihail, the daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
NLT.19: Mahalath had three sons — Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
NLT.20: Later Rehoboam married another cousin, Maacah, the granddaughter of Absalom. Maacah gave birth to Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
NLT.21: Rehoboam loved Maacah more than any of his other wives and concubines. In all, he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and they gave birth to twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
NLT.22: Rehoboam appointed Maacah’s son Abijah as leader among the princes, making it clear that he would be the next king.
NLT.23: Rehoboam also wisely gave responsibilities to his other sons and stationed some of them in the fortified towns throughout the land of Judah and Benjamin. He provided them with generous provisions, and he found many wives for them.

CSB17.1: When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, <sup>ⓓ</sup> he mobilized the house of Judah and Benjamin — one hundred eighty thousand fit young soldiers — to fight against Israel to restore the reign to Rehoboam.
CSB17.2: But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, <sup>ⓔ</sup> the man of God:
CSB17.3: “Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people:
CSB17.4: ‘This is what the LORD says: You are not to march up and fight against your brothers. <sup>ⓕ</sup> Each of you return home, for this incident has come from me.’” <sup>ⓖ</sup> So they listened to what the LORD said and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
CSB17.5: Rehoboam stayed in Jerusalem, and he fortified cities <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓗ</sup> in Judah.
CSB17.6: He built up Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
CSB17.10: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are fortified cities in Judah and in Benjamin.
CSB17.11: He strengthened their fortifications and put leaders in them with supplies of food, oil, and wine.
CSB17.12: He also put large shields and spears in each and every city to make them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.
CSB17.13: The priests and Levites from all their regions throughout Israel took their stand with Rehoboam,
CSB17.14: for the Levites left their pasturelands and their possessions <sup>ⓘ</sup> and went to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons refused to let them serve as priests of the LORD. <sup>ⓙ</sup>

CSB17.18: Rehoboam married Mahalath, daughter of David’s son Jerimoth and of Abihail daughter of Jesse’s son Eliab. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.19: She bore sons to him: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
CSB17.20: After her, he married Maacah daughter <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓑ</sup> of Absalom. She bore Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith to him.
CSB17.21: Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines. He acquired eighteen wives <sup>ⓒ</sup> and sixty concubines and was the father of twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
CSB17.22: Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief, leader among his brothers, intending to make him king. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.23: Rehoboam also showed discernment by dispersing some of his sons to all the regions of Judah and Benjamin and to all the fortified cities. He gave them plenty of provisions and sought many wives for them.

NIV.5:
Rehoboam Fortifies Judah

NIV.10: Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron. These were fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin.

Rehoboam’s Family
Rehoboam married Mahalath, who was the daughter of David’s son Jerimoth and of Abihail, the daughter of Jesse’s son Eliab.
NIV.19: She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.
NIV.20: Then he married Maacah daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
NIV.21: Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than any of his other wives and concubines. In all, he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
